target_customer: Health systems, hospitals and public programs launching large scale genomic testing programs (customer logos on site include Geisinger, Mount Sinai, Dana-Farber and the State of Florida)
problem: Health systems struggle to triage, consent, order and follow up on genetic tests inside the EHR, so genetic results rarely change care. Nest provides lab agnostic software with EHR integrated decision support.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to health systems and genomic programs (pricing not found)
product_category: Clinical genomics software and clinical decision support

founders.name: Moran Snir
prior_employers: Invitae (led Software and Data after acquisition of Clear Genetics)
education: BA and MSc in biomedical engineering
previous_startups: MorNetware, maker of Genometer carrier screening software
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page; she is a two time YC alum.

founders.name: Guy Snir
education: MBA, Duke and Tel Aviv University
previous_startups: Clear Genetics (W17, co-founder and COO, acquired by Invitae)

competitors.name: My Gene Counsel
competitors.what: Genetic variant and decision support content, partnering with Genomet for precision cancer care decision support

technical_complexity.rationale: EHR integration (SMART on FHIR), lab agnostic ordering and rule based decision support are hard integration work but standard engineering; rule based tools avoid FDA clearance per press.

defensibility.rationale: Deep EHR and lab integrations and clinical workflows create switching costs, and founders had prior success with the same buyers at Clear Genetics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Nest partnered with Genome Medical rather than being copied, and remains independent per 2026 profiles.

market_need_then: Genetic testing volume was rising while health systems lacked tools to deliver counseling and decision support at scale; the company's seed announcement cited expansion to pediatrics, polygenic risk and pharmacogenetics.

branding.name_origin: Not stated directly. CEO Moran Snir said in funding coverage that Nest is thought of as your home for genetic information.
branding.domain_note: Uses nestgenomics.com, not nest.com (taken by a well known thermostat brand); no history found.

identity.logo: Logo image on the site; design not described by sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and mission driven: Make genomic care part of every patient journey

brand_strength.rationale: The name is warm and fits the home for genetic information idea, but it is generic, collides with Nest Health and the thermostat brand, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Founders who had already sold Clear Genetics to Invitae in 2019 built Nest in 2021 and joined YC in Winter 2022, then closed an $8.5M seed led by B Capital in January 2023. The product reports health system and state customers and EHR and lab integrations, and no layoffs, Series A or exit were found, so the company appears to be an independent, growing enterprise software business.
notes: Seed confirmed by Business Wire and MedCity News; Caplight lists about $9M total and Extruct gives a range, treated as aggregator noise. Other plausible rivals (Genome Medical, InformedDNA, Color) were found only on undated pages, so they are not listed. No Series A found as of 2026 searches.
